transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-05-12
- Start: 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Miles (Verdant Head of ML), Maya Singh (Verdant Platform), Liam O'Connor (Verdant Security), Ava Chen (Verdant Product)

Auto-summary (brief):
Verdant is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing knowledge assistant that needs long-context (20k-32k), multilingual support for EN/ES/FR, and tool-calling to query internal inventory and run small DB lookups. Primary concerns: latency under 350ms p50 for short prompts, predictable unit cost, and corporate security controls (KMS, SAML, audit logs).

[00:00] Jordan Hale: hey everyone, thanks for doing this. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. quick round-robin?
[00:08] Ethan Miles: Ethan here, head of ML at Verdant. we're trying to pick a path for inference — whether hosted is fine, or we need dedicated or private for regulatory and latency reasons.
[00:15] Maya Singh: Maya, platform. I'll be the one setting up any network peering or infra if we go dedicated/private.
[00:19] Liam O'Connor: Liam, security. focused on encryption, key mgmt, audit trails.
[00:22] Ava Chen: Ava, product. primarily care about multilingual quality and tooling for agents calling our inventory API.

[00:36] Priya Nair: great. quick agenda: model fit (open models), context length and retrieval, tool-calling/function-calling, deployment tradeoffs, and next steps. sound ok?
[00:45] Ethan: yes. starting with models — we have a mix of short Q&A and long document summarization (policy docs). a lot of our users will paste 10–20 page docs. so context is big. also multi-lingual, Spanish + French heavy.

[01:10] Priya: got it. for long docs we usually look at 32k+ context models or a retrieval approach with chunking plus KV/prefix caching. on open models you mentioned — are you biased toward any family?
[01:20] Ethan: we've used a custom Llama 3 variant in-house but ops cost exploded. curious about Mistral, Llama-3, and whatever Redwood curates. also we'd like to try quantized variants for cost.

[01:40] Jordan: Redwood maintains a catalog of verified model profiles — open models and optimized variants. for 32k we have tuned variants that keep latency predictable; for cost-savings we recommend quantized 4-bit for non-critical outputs, or mixed precision. tradeoff is output flavor and sometimes slight regen patterns.

[02:05] Ava: tool-calling is big for us — our assistant needs to call inventory and a pricing microservice. how mature is your function-calling support? can it be used with private deployments?
[02:18] Priya: we support structured function-calling and tool orchestration across hosted/dedicated/private. function schema mapping works the same. on private we run the control plane in a customer VPC or on-prem so calls can reach internal services via peered network — but there are firewall and NAT considerations.

[02:42] Liam: on the security side, we need SAML SSO, RBAC audit logs, and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). is that available in Redwood Private?
[02:53] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integration and HSM options for keys; audit logs and longer retention are add-ons. SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning is supported in enterprise tiers. we'll send the security pack after the call.

[03:10] Ethan: latency — we want p50 for short queries under 350ms, p95 under 800ms ideally. can hosted meet that?
[03:21] Priya: depends on model and region. hosted with our low-latency endpoints can hit ~200–300ms for small context using distilled/optimized models. for consistent latency at scale we recommend Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and pinned model variants. Private gives you maximum isolation but ops overhead.

[03:44] Maya: what about cost? rough differences between hosted and dedicated?
[03:48] Jordan: rough rule: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing and is easiest to start; Dedicated is committed-capacity with a monthly reservation — lower per-token costs at scale but requires commit. Private has platform fees plus infra. we'll share a back-of-envelope cost comparison.

[04:12] Ethan: multilingual performance — do you benchmark for ES/FR? or is it best to do our own evals?
[04:20] Priya: we have canned evals and multi-lingual traces, but your domain prompts matter. recommended approach: run a short eval with your prompt set across 2–3 candidate models (e.g., Llama-3-32k tuned, Mistral-Extended, Redwood-2-32k) — measure accuracy, hallucination, latency. we can run this as a 1-week benchmark.

[04:50] Ava: on hallucination, we need consistent factuality for policy docs. does Redwood provide retrieval+tooling for grounding?
[04:58] Priya: yes — built-in retrieval connectors and a reranker pipeline; plus prefix/KV caching can reduce re-computation for repeated doc contexts. you'll likely pair retrieval for large docs and use 32k models for single-prompt full-doc summaries when needed.

[05:20] Ethan: cool. for the bench, we want to test: 1) 32k summarization, 2) multi-turn Q&A with tool calls, 3) multi-lingual prompts. what do you need from us?
[05:30] Priya: sample prompts (10–15), 3 full doc examples, expected correctness metrics, and a small test harness or API keys — we can take your prompts and run on hosted first then on a Dedicated trial cluster.

[05:44] Maya: network — if we do Dedicated or Private, what peering patterns do you expect? is there a simple VPC peering flow?
[05:51] Jordan: for Dedicated we do secure peering or private link depending on cloud. for Private we provide an ops package that walks through VPC peering, route tables and firewall rules. Priya will send the exact list of ports and IP ranges.

[06:05] Liam: about logs — do we get token-level or request-level logs and can they be sent to our SIEM?
[06:11] Priya: request-level telemetry and trace hooks are available; token-level cost breakpoint summaries are in console. For Private we can ship logs to your SIEM via secure endpoints; for hosted we support secure log forwarding with redaction options.

[06:30] Ethan: curious about model failover — if you lose capacity for the 32k tuned variant, can requests auto-fallback to smaller models gracefully?
[06:40] Jordan: yes, smart routing supports fallback policies — you can set graceful degrade to a cheaper model or queued retry. plus you can pin fallbacks per route.

[06:55] Ava: edge case — we need to run a tool that executes a small SQL query and returns structured JSON; does Redwood's tool-calling keep strict schema enforcement?
[07:05] Priya: function-calling enforces schemas and the runtime can validate outputs. we can also run a small shim in your network for verification if you want extra control.

[07:20] Ethan: what about fine-tuning vs eval prompts? we've thought about a small fine-tune on our support data. is it necessary?
[07:27] Priya: often prompt engineering + retrieval is sufficient. fine-tune or RLHF can be used for very specific behaviors, but it increases ops and model lineage. we usually recommend starting with prompt engineering and a small eval to see the gap.

[07:45] Jordan: recap and recommended pilot: 1) run 1-week benchmark on hosted for three candidate models (your prompts) to measure latency/cost/accuracy; 2) if latency variance is too high, spin up a 2-week Dedicated trial with reserved GPU pool for the tuned 32k variant; 3) security pack + SAML/KMS design review for Private if needed.

[08:10] Maya: timeline: we want results in two weeks; also need cost estimates to present to finance.
[08:15] Jordan: we'll aim to share pricing ranges and the security pack within 48 hours; Priya will share the benchmark plan and required artifacts.

[08:30] Ava: one last Q — does Redwood support A/B testing of model/quantization variants in production?
[08:36] Priya: yes — rollouts, canary, and automatic fallback are supported in Redwood Console. you can route percentages per-model and collect metrics.

[08:48] Liam: good. let's get the security docs and SSO flow.
[08:52] Jordan: will do. thanks everyone.

Outro notes: call ended with agreement to exchange sample prompts and security docs. Verdant to review pricing once received.
